input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.4.2 confirms that the fixed sums payable by PB on termination under Section 14.2 are "in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have" — i.e., they are liquidated amounts payable by us, the Customer, and are therefore squarely within this rule (SFJ's contingent Approval Payments under Article 6, and the optional Buy-Out Payments under Section 6.7, are the priced commercial bargain and are not flagged). Two of those liquidated amounts fail the fallback on a material term: (i) Section 14.2.1 requires PB to pay 300% of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ (up to roughly $360M against the $120M funding benchmark in Section 6.2) within days of a breach termination, while PB also remains liable for Approval Payments; and (ii) Section 14.2.10 adds 25% per annum interest to a termination triggered not by any breach but by PB's good-faith exercise of its own decision-making authority under Section 5.2.4 — punitive amounts triggered by non-material or non-breach events, which is walk-away territory. Given the financing structure, deleting the payment entirely (preferred position) would be disproportionate, so our redline takes the smallest step: return of the Development Costs SFJ actually funded (the same measure SFJ already accepted in Section 14.2.9), with the punitive 3x multiple and 25% uplift removed. We have not separately reopened the 150%/300% figures in Sections 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7 or 14.2.8.1, which should be conformed if this principle is accepted.

proposal.summary: Remove punitive multiple and default interest from PB's termination payments (return of SFJ's actual Development Costs only)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we do not pay liquidated damages or penalties, so we have reduced the 300% multiple on a breach termination to a return of the Development Costs SFJ actually funded and deleted the 25% per annum uplift on a JSC-decision termination. These fixed sums are expressly in lieu of damages under Section 14.4.2, so a 3x multiple and 25% interest operate as a penalty rather than compensation; we are happy to keep the exclusive-remedy construct in exchange.

ops.oldText: an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
ops.newText: an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination

ops.oldText: an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ plus interest at the annual rate of twenty-five percent (25%) from the date such Development Costs were paid or incurred by SFJ
ops.newText: an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ
